review_items.concrete_reason: The south-west door opens into an unobstructed south lane: tv_bench_media is well north of the door clearance, coffee_table_main begins beyond the incoming route, and sofa_main is on the opposite east wall.

The rendered route targets reach sofa_main, tv_bench_media, armchair_reading, and coffee_table_main from the entry. The south lane feeds the west media access, then the open central lane branches to the sofa and the north reading position.

sofa_main has a clear west-facing sitting approach separated from coffee_table_main; tv_bench_media is reachable from the entry-side lane; and armchair_reading has an open south-west approach while side_table_reading and floor_lamp_reading remain out of its sit-down footprint.

sofa_main, tv_bench_media, and coffee_table_main form the media-and-conversation axis. armchair_reading, side_table_reading, and floor_lamp_reading form a compact north reading perch rather than being distributed as unrelated decorative objects.

The two largest pieces are constrained to opposite walls, leaving a continuous south entry lane and a broad central passage. armchair_reading uses the north interior without crowding the north window clearance.

sofa_main faces tv_bench_media across the room and coffee_table_main sits in reachable shared space rather than blocking the doorway. armchair_reading is turned toward its open approach and the social zone, not directly into the north wall or window.

The east-wall sofa and opposing media bench establish the primary room axis. coffee_table_main is a subordinate shared surface, while armchair_reading is visibly a smaller secondary activity zone at the north side.

The closest living_room_004 puts tv_bench_01 on the west-south side and serves its east-wall sofa with both side_table_01 and floor_lamp_01. This scene instead makes a north reading trio around armchair_reading, centers tv_bench_media on the west wall, offsets coffee_table_main southward, and has a ten-edge frozen partner graph with only 0.333333 graph similarity.
